lowDistraction: Try to restrain yourself from drinking coffee, caffeinated tea, and soda, and start to drink decaffeinated beverages as a replacement, such as natural fruit-based tea, juice, caffeine-free soda, or simply water.

-Set a time on your phone where it locks you out of entertainment apps, such as YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, etc. to stop yourself from using your phone late. And, in the case that you must use your phone before bed or at night, turn on night mode and set your brightness to the lowest.

-Create a consistent bedtime routine not by forcing yourself to sleep at a specific time, but by forcing yourself to wake up 12+ hours before the time that you want to fall asleep. By continuing to do so, a good sleep schedule will form for you naturally. If you are looking for a way to fix your sleep schedule in a smoother way, you can wake up earlier than your usual time by 30-60 minute intervals each night.
lowMentalHealth: Try to create a habit of doing a calming activity before going to sleep.
Doing this not only increases your sleep quality, but it also reinforces your health, both physical and mental.
Reading, doing breathing exercises, stretches, meditation, etc. can be very beneficial for you, even if it is only for 10-15 minutes a day.

Instead of overthinking your future, or ruminating over a decision you regret not making in the past, try to think of something calming, like a walk along the shoreline, or a snowy winter night. You could also try to feel what is going on around you. What you are hearing, what you are feeling, what you smell, etc. By not taking the time to wind down before bed, you are trying to stop a train going at full speed instantly. You have to make sure that you are not full of energy and active before going to bed, as not only is that bad for your sleep quality, but it is also bad for your mental health.
lowSleepDeficiency: You're life is being impacted by your poor sleep.
